findings.text: _owned_projects composes its own terminal-phase set, including the launch-failed exclusion, at project granularity instead of asking live_work_run at pair granularity. A project that holds live work for one owned session is enumerated, and then every owned session in it is asked the pane judgement: live_work_populations treats launch-failed as non-terminal, so a pair whose only pointer is launch-failed starts a follower as soon as another owned session holds live work in the same project. That contradicts done_when case 3, which says a launch-failed pointer starts no follower, and the section's statement that the scan composes no scan or terminal set of its own. The case-3 test cannot observe it because its fixture leaves the project unenumerated.

The done_when names eight negative controls and negative-controls.log records three: dropping the mark in parse_request, admitting unmarked previous children, and skipping the start-up scan. The five unrun controls are dropping _remove_fifo from SessionHost.stop, matching only the current session, ignoring the phase, ignoring the session, and filtering on session_id instead of session. The unrun 'ignoring the phase' control is exactly the one that would have exposed the pair-level launch-failed gap, so the assertion at this line is green partly because the project enumeration filtered the fixture out before the pane judgement was asked.

The neighbouring-tests.log header names revision e5179a465f while its '# tree' line is the head worktree, so the log that is offered as proof the importing test files add no failure states a revision it did not run at. The work itself is sound (24 passed, EXIT=0) but the header cannot be reconciled from the log alone.
